summary: Converts a rotation vector a2 (3-vector plus angle magnitude in a2[3]) into a quaternion-shaped output a1 whose scalar part is always written as 0.0. For angle >= 1.0 or near-singular sin(angle) the vector part is copied verbatim; otherwise the vector part is scaled by angle/sin(angle).

local_names.a2: input rotation vector (x, y, z, angle)
local_names.v8: angle copied into float temp for division

operations.description: If a2[3] >= 1.0 (angle magnitude threshold), skip the sin-scaled path and copy the input vector part verbatim.
FloatFunctionPassThrough() is invoked before computing sin(angle); its effect is not evident from the raw source.
Compute v7 = sin(angle), then derive the scale factor v6 = angle / v7 when the near-zero check passes.
FloatRangeCheck(sin(angle), 0.0) detects a near-singular angle; when it reports the sine as zero, the vector part is copied verbatim instead of scaled.
Verbatim path: copy the input vector into the output a1[0]=a2[0], a1[1]=a2[1], a1[2]=a2[2].
Scaled path: write the vector part of the output as angle/sin(angle) times the input vector (a1[0], a1[1], a1[2]).
On both paths the scalar part of the output is written as a1[3] = 0.0.

clean_pseudocode: out[0] = scale * in[0]; out[1] = scale * in[1]; out[2] = scale * in[2];
